REAX Engine server (reax13 mode, the maker's release code), self-hosted, FP8

Two models run together, option probabilities averaged 50/50: 57.36B in all, all used on every question. two full models: part G (Gemma 4 31B line, with vision encoder) + part Q (Qwen3.8-27B line, with vision encoder and 255-way readout); source: counted from the checkpoint's safetensors, decisionmodels/REAX-1.3@fa4bf7e, huggingface.co/decisionmodels/REAX-1.3; read 9 November 2026

REAX's released REAX 1.3 weights (decisionmodels/REAX-1.3 at fa4bf7e), a decision model of two parts that both score every question; each option's probability is the 50/50 mean of the two parts'. Part G blends CharlieBT/gx31-decider (Gemma line, from tattrongvu/Jeffan-31b-1710) with PelaAI/KnowLine-31B-Gen1 (Gemma-4-31B); part Q blends gurujustin/sn92-gen-p5 (Qwen3.5-27B line, through baselabs/mammoth-1) with vllm-sr/d3-ultra. The model card calls REAX a decentralised lab on Bittensor subnet 92. It ran on our hardware through the maker's engine (the reax13 mode of reaxlabs/reax-engine at ff8f595, its own server, serve.py), both parts in FP8 (block-128) on one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, text only, one request at a time. Its card lists English only.

Latency: the time from sending one request to receiving its answer, measured from our computer, network and any retries within the request included. Request time: the time at least one request was in flight, over the requests whose answers were kept. It is not the run's elapsed time: it leaves out requests that failed and any pause before a run was resumed.
